nodes.summary: Let $a$ be a string of $n$ positive integers, let $p$, $q'$ and $q$ be the upper-right, lower-left and lower-right entries of its convergent matrix $C(a)$, and let $\overleftarrow{a}$ be the reverse of $a$. Then the Gauss–Kuzmin masses satisfy $P_{GK}(a) = P_{GK}(\overleftarrow{a})$ and $P_{GK}(a) = \left|\log_2\left(1 + \frac{(-1)^n}{(p + q)(q' + q)}\right)\right|$.
nodes.title: Explicit Gauss–Kuzmin mass of a string

nodes.summary: Write $P_{GK}$ for the Gauss–Kuzmin mass and $\chi$ for the characteristic number of a string. If $a$ and $b$ are strings of positive integers whose lengths have the same parity, then $P_{GK}(a) = P_{GK}(b)$ if and only if $\chi(a) = \chi(b)$.
nodes.title: Gauss–Kuzmin masses agree exactly when characteristic numbers do

nodes.summary: The Gauss–Kuzmin mass of the empty string is $P_{GK}(()) = \frac{1}{\log 2} \int_{[0, 1)} \frac{dx}{1 + x}$.

nodes.summary: For a finite string $a$ of natural numbers with fundamental interval $I(a)$, the Gauss–Kuzmin mass of $a$ is $P_{GK}(a) = \frac{1}{\log 2} \int_{I(a)} \frac{dx}{1 + x}$, the measure of $I(a)$ under the Gauss–Kuzmin measure with density $\frac{1}{(1 + x) \log 2}$.

nodes.summary: A finite string $a$ of natural numbers has a nontrivial symmetry if there is a string $b$ that is a rearrangement of $a$ (the same entries with the same multiplicities, in some order) such that $b \ne a$, $b$ is not the reverse of $a$, and $P_{GK}(b) = P_{GK}(a)$, where $P_{GK}$ denotes the Gauss–Kuzmin measure of a string.

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ and let $N \ge 1$. For a string $a$ of positive integers write $I(a)$ for its fundamental interval, $P_{GK}(a)$ for its Gauss–Kuzmin measure and $a^{\mathrm{rev}}$ for its reverse. If $\mu(I(a)) = P_{GK}(a)$ for every string $a$ of exactly $N$ positive integers, then $\mu(I(a)) = \mu(I(a^{\mathrm{rev}}))$ for every string $a$ of at most $N$ positive integers.
nodes.title: Reversal symmetry from agreement with the Gauss–Kuzmin measure

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $a = (a_1, \dots, a_n)$ be a stable string of positive integers. Put $a^+ = (2, 1, a_1, \dots, a_{n-1}, a_n + 1)$ and $\sigma(a^+) = (2, a_n + 1, a_{n-1}, \dots, a_1, 1)$. Then $\sigma(a^+)$ is a rearrangement of $a^+$, it differs both from $a^+$ and from the reverse of $a^+$, and $P_{GK}(\sigma(a^+)) = P_{GK}(a^+)$, where $P_{GK}$ denotes the Gauss–Kuzmin measure of a string.
